article_manifest.title: Mali: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches - What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed (African Arguments)
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches - What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed (African Arguments)
article_manifest.summary: The mutiny that broke out in air base 101 in Niamey in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the 'jihadists.' For all of the Sahel, it's a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.

article_manifest.summary: Thanks to the use of precise intelligence, the Malian Armed Forces continue their missions of surveillance and security of the national territory image illustration The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) continue their operations of surveillance, reconnaissance and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the exploitation of precise information allowed the units involved to locate a group of motorcyclists in the Ouagadou forest, near the village of Ngoma Koura.

article_manifest.title: Mali: Youssouf Toloba and Dan Na Ambassagou reaffirm their commitment to the homeland, peace and national unity
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : Youssouf Toloba et Dan Na Ambassagou réaffirment leur engagement pour la patrie, la paix et l’unité nationale
article_manifest.summary: Youssouf Toloba and Dan Na Ambassagou: a call for peace and the strengthening of security in Mali. Faced with disputed information about his alleged encirclement, Dan Na Ambassagou's Chief of Staff enjoys the support of his movement. In Bandiagara, hunters are calling for increased security, better coordination with FAMa and increased attention from Transitional Authorities .

article_manifest.title: Two European Hostages Freed in Niger
article_manifest.original_title: Two European Hostages Freed in Niger
article_manifest.summary: Two European women abducted in Niger in 2025 have been released after spending more than a year in captivity, according to Libyan media reports. Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian citizen Claudia Abbt, 69, arrived in the eastern Libyan city of Benghazi following their release. Libya’s eastern-based Al-Masar TV reported that the two women had been freed after being held hostage in Niger for about a year and a half.

article_manifest.title: Niger-Algeria military cooperation: a new strategic partnership for the security of the Sahel and regional sovereignty
article_manifest.original_title: Coopération militaire Niger-Algérie : un nouveau partenariat stratégique au service de la sécurité du Sahel et de la souveraineté régionale
article_manifest.summary: The signing of a military cooperation protocol between Niamey and Algiers marks a new stage in the rapprochement between the two countries. Faced with cross-border security challenges, this initiative opens up prospects for consultation and collaboration, in a region where States intend to have greater control over their strategic choices and strengthen their defence capacities BAMADA.NET - Regional cooperation in the field of defence remains a major issue for Sahel-Saharan countries.

article_manifest.title: Military cooperation: a delegation of the Turkish gendarmerie in immersion at the gendarmerie of Burkina
article_manifest.original_title: Coopération militaire: une délégation de la gendarmerie turque en immersion a la gendarmerie du Burkina
article_manifest.summary: A delegation of the Turkish gendarmerie is staying in Ouagadougou, as part of a working visit and consolidation of the partnership with the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso. This mission is led by Lieutenant General Aykut Tanriverdi, Deputy Commander of the General Command of the Gendarmerie of the Republic of Türkiye It is with the rise of colors, an act highly solemn and rich in symbols that the Turkish delegation began its immersion within the National Gendarmerie of Burkina Faso .

article_manifest.title: Niger-Libya: Eva Gretzmacher and Claudia Abbt released and arrived in Benghazi
article_manifest.original_title: Niger–Libye : Eva Gretzmacher et Claudia Abbt libérées et arrivées à Benghazi
article_manifest.summary: Austria's Eva Gretzmacher and Switzerland's Claudia Abbt, kidnapped separately in Agadez in 2025, were released and arrived in Benghazi, eastern Libya, on Wednesday, 21 October. Their submission to the Austrian and Swiss authorities must take place after the completion of the necessary formalities . According to our information, a plane was to leave Benghazi on Thursday, October 22, stop in Vienna to hand over Eva Gretzmacher to the Austrian authorities, then continue to Switzerland with Claudia Abbt.

article_manifest.original_title: Macina : fin du blocus à Tongolo coura
article_manifest.summary: The inhabitants of Tongolo Coura, in the municipality of Kolongo, Macina circle, have been freely going about their business again for a week. According to villagers, the village is no longer under blockade after several years of restrictions imposed by unidentified armed men. Dozo hunters defended the town.

article_manifest.summary: Reinstating the death penalty in Burkina Faso risks being used to "crack down on dissent", according to HRW The reinstatement of the death penalty in Burkina Faso is a "chilling message" to opponents in the junta-ruled country and risks being used as "a new tool to crack down on dissent", human rights NGO Human Rights Watch (HRW) warned on Wednesday. . Burkina is led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, who came to power after a military coup in September 2022.

article_manifest.title: KAYES: two alleged fuel suppliers to the Armed Terrorist Groups arrested by the Police
article_manifest.original_title: KAYES: deux présumés fournisseurs de carburant aux Groupes Armés Terroristes interpellés par la Police
article_manifest.summary: The elements of the Police Station of the 2nd district of Kayes proceeded, on Friday 16 and Sunday 18 October 2026, to the arrest of two individuals suspected of supplying the Armed Terrorist Groups with fuel . These operations are part of the sustained efforts made by the regional authorities, in synergy with the Defence and Security Forces (FDS), to dismantle the logistical support networks for the Armed Terrorist Groups (AGTS) and to hinder their supply chains .

article_manifest.title: Military cooperation: Algeria and Niger sign a partnership agreement
article_manifest.original_title: Coopération militaire : l'Algérie et le Niger signent un accord de partenariat
article_manifest.summary: Algeria and Niger want to strengthen their exchanges in the field of defence. This Wednesday, October 21, in Algiers, Chief of Staff Saïd Chanegriha and that of Niger, Salifou Modi signed a memorandum of understanding on military cooperation between the two countries. Said Chanegriha, expressed the readiness of the Algerian army to examine any Nigerian proposal aimed at consolidating their military and security relations .

article_manifest.original_title: Agadez : Inhumation des corps d’une douzaine de victimes de l’attaque armée sur l’axe Arlit-Agadez
article_manifest.summary: Agadez, Oct. 21 (ANP) – The Governor of the Agadez Region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa attended, on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, the removal of the bodies, followed by the burial of the victims of the attack against the SONITRAV buses on the Arlit–Agadez axis.

article_manifest.title: Fight against terrorism, Burkina Faso reinstates the death penalty
article_manifest.original_title: Lutte contre le terrorisme, le Burkina Faso rétablit la peine de mort
article_manifest.summary: The Government of Burkina Faso had put forward the idea in the Council of Ministers on 4 December. Nearly a year later, the transitional parliament unanimously voted on a new penal code that reinstates the death penalty, although it has been abolished since May 2018. Acts of terrorism, espionage, treason, or even parricide and the import of expired or prohibited products, resulting in death, are punishable by death.

article_manifest.title: Burkina: the death penalty reintroduced in the Penal Code
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina: la peine de mort réintroduite dans le Code pénal
article_manifest.summary: The People's Legislative Assembly of Burkina Faso adopted, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the draft law on the Penal Code, thus enacting the reintroduction of the death penalty, which had been abolished in 2018. The draft law revising Law No. 025-2018/AN of May 25, 2018 on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso was adopted on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, by the People's Legislative Assembly .

article_manifest.original_title: Insécurité : les autorités d’Agadez en état d’alerte maximale après une attaque armée qui a fait douze morts sur l’axe Tchiro-Agadez
article_manifest.summary: The Governor of the Agadez region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa, chaired an emergency meeting of the Regional Security Council (CRS) on Wednesday, 21 October 2026. Several items were on the agenda of the forum, including, among others, the examination and analysis of the security situation in the region, with a particular focus on the attack on the two SONITRAV buses, which occurred on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, on the Tchirozérine-Agadez.

article_manifest.title: Niger: two Western hostages released in Libya after more than a year and a half at the hands of the Islamic State
article_manifest.original_title: Niger : deux otages occidentales libérées en Libye après plus d’un an et demi aux mains de l’État islamique
article_manifest.summary: Niger : deux otages occidentales libérées en Libye après plus d’un an et demi aux mains de l’État islamique Détenues au Niger par l’État islamique pendant plus d’un an et demi, Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher ont été libérées et sont arrivées à Benghazi. La médiation a été orchestrée par Saddam Haftar, désireux d’asseoir son influence politique au Sahel. C’est la fin d’un long calvaire pour Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher.

article_manifest.title: Transition Support Fund: The moto-taximan Dramane Kamiya makes a contribution of 100,000 CFA francs
article_manifest.original_title: Fonds de soutien à la Transition : Le moto-taximan Dramane Kamiya apporte une contribution de 100.000 Fcfa
article_manifest.summary: Bamako, October 21, 2026 (AMAP)– Dramane Kamiya, a 49-year-old motorcycle taxi driver, contributed 100,000 FCFA to the Transition Support Fund. He presented his donation on Wednesday to the Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, during a ceremony organized at the Primature, noted AMAP . A father living in Badalabougou, the donor explained that he wanted to contribute to national recovery efforts, despite the modesty of his daily income.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: Parliament Votes To Restore Capital Punishment
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso: Parliament Votes To Restore Capital Punishment
article_manifest.summary: By Enyichukwu Enemanna Burkina Faso’s parliament on Tuesday adopted a revised penal code that reinstates death penalty, nearly a decade after it was abolished in the West African country, the Justice Ministry said in a statement. The revised penal code reintroduces the death penalty for crimes including terrorism, espionage, treason and importing expired or banned products that result in death, government-owned news organisations said.

article_manifest.original_title: Opération Dougoukoloko : plusieurs éléments terroristes neutralisés dans la Forêt de Ouagadou

article_manifest.title: Ten suspects arrested in an alleged QNET case

article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso : le Parlement adopte le rétablissement de la peine de mort

The new Code was passed on 20 October 2026, eight years after the abolition of the death penalty in the country . The Minister of Justice, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, justifies this reform by the need to modernize the legal framework, strengthen security, fight against terrorism and protect populations.

article_manifest.title: Benbere platform fights disinformation in Mali
article_manifest.original_title: La plateforme Benbere lutte contre la désinformation au Mali
article_manifest.summary: It is increasingly difficult for young people, in the Sahel countries as elsewhere, to distinguish between information and disinformation. Young people are really at the heart of the dynamics of fake news because they are, first of all, the main target, on social networks that have become the main source of information for adolescents and young adults But young people are also key players in the fight against disinformation.

article_manifest.original_title: Forêt de Ouagadou : Les FAMa neutralisent une importante colonne terroriste

The Executive Office of the Idaksahak community accuses elements of the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS). This violence occurs in the context of clashes between rival armed groups in the region.

article_manifest.title: Mali: Violence in the centre of the country - “We fled by canoe in the middle of the night”
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: Violences dans le centre du pays - « Nous avons fui en pirogue au milieu de la nuit »
article_manifest.summary: Depuis le début du mois de septembre, le centre du Mali est le théâtre d'une recrudescence des violences qui a fait des dizaines de victimes et provoqué le déplacement de milliers de personnes. Face à ce nouveau flux de déplacés, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) a mis en place une clinique mobile dans la ville de Macina, où converge un grand nombre de familles.

article_manifest.title: Massacre in Mali: Islamic State attacks the Idaksahak community in the Menaka region
article_manifest.original_title: Massacre au Mali : l’État islamique s’attaque à la communauté idaksahak dans la région de Ménaka
article_manifest.summary: Massacre in Mali: Islamic State Tackles Idaksahak Community in Menaka Region The Islamic State terrorist attack claimed the lives of at least 48 civilians in the Menaka region of Mali. This massacre, targeting the Idaksahak community and perpetrated in retaliation for military operations, marks a tragic escalation. At least 48 civilians were killed by fighters of the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISS) (ex-Islamic State in the Greater Sahara) on Sunday, October 18, in Tagadayat, in the Menaka region of northeastern Mali.

article_manifest.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men (security and local sources)
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: plus d'une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés (sources sécuritaires et locales)
article_manifest.summary: More than 40 civilians were killed on Sunday in attacks by armed men in the Menaka region of northeastern Mali, causing population displacement, several security, local and associative sources told AFP on Monday. These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arrived on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, came.

article_manifest.title: Militants Kill 50 Civilians in Mali in Retaliation for 'Azawad Movement'
article_manifest.original_title: مسلحون يقتلون 50 مدنيا في مالي انتقاما من "حركة أزواد"
article_manifest.summary: ملخص قال مصدر أمني إن المسلحين "أطلقوا النار على كل ما يتحرك، وقُتل 50 مدنياً، بينهم شباب وكبار في السن"، مشيراً إلى أن نازحين فروا من العنف بدأوا بالوصول إلى ميناكا أمس الإثنين، وتحدث مسؤول محلي عن عدد أكبر من القتلى، قائلاً إن الحصيلة "تتخطى 50 قتيلاً، بينهم نساء وكبار في السن". قُتل 50 مدنياً بهجمات شنها مسلحون نهاية الأسبوع الماضي على مخيمات في منطقة ميناكا شمال شرقي مالي، وفق ما أفادت مصادر أمنية وأخرى محلية وكالة الصحافة الفرنسية أمس الإثنين.

article_manifest.title: Macina hosts more than 3,400 displaced people after the September violence
article_manifest.original_title: Macina accueille plus de 3 400 déplacés après les violences de septembre
article_manifest.summary: RIGHT NOW More than 3,400 displaced people have reached Macina after the violence that occurred in September in several localities in the Ségou region, according to a report published on 16 October by Médecins Sans Frontières. MSF cites an attack in Souleye on September 1 and another in Touara on September 15. The identity of the authors and the complete human toll remain to be established .

article_manifest.title: More than 40 civilians killed in armed attack in northeast Mali
article_manifest.original_title: مقتل أكثر من 40 مدنيا في هجوم مسلح شمال شرقي مالي
article_manifest.summary: More than 40 civilians have been killed in attacks by militants on camps in Mali's northeastern Menaka region, AFP quoted security and local sources as saying. The sources reported that the attackers used motorcycles to reach camps inhabited mostly by members of the Dussaq tribe, whose executive body accused the Islamic State of being behind the killings. According to the sources, the Dussac tribe is the cradle of the armed “Movement for the Salvation of Azawad”, allied with the government, in Bamako.

article_manifest.title: Kati: a prayer session in memory of the victims of the crisis
article_manifest.original_title: Kati : une séance de prières en mémoire des victimes de la crise
article_manifest.summary: The Minister of Religious Affairs, Worship and Customs, Dr. Mahamadou Koné, took part, on Sunday, October 18, 2026 in Kati, in a prayer and sacrifice session organized by the military hierarchy in memory of the civilian and military victims of the crisis in Mali . The ceremony was attended by Major General Oumar Diarra, Minister Delegate to the Minister of Defence, military officials and bereaved families.

article_manifest.title: Defence and Security: 678 young soldiers trained and presented to the flag in Koutiala
article_manifest.original_title: Défense et Sécurité : 678 jeunes soldats formés et présentés au drapeau à Koutiala
article_manifest.summary: Brigadier General Harouna Samaké, Governor of the Koutiala region, today formalized the end of the training course for 678 soldiers of contingent 2025, in a ceremony marked by the presentation to the flag. After six months of Basic Common Training (FCB), these 678 recruits – out of the 680 initially hired – have successfully completed their course .

article_manifest.title: Justice: Opening of the combined hearings of the correctional and criminal chambers of the Military Court of Mopti
article_manifest.original_title: Justice : Ouverture des audiences couplées des chambres correctionnelle et criminelle du Tribunal militaire de Mopti
article_manifest.summary: Mopti, October 20 (AMAP) The work of the combined hearings of the correctional chamber and the criminal chamber of the Military Court (TM) of Mopti, for the year 2026, began on Monday, October 19, 2026, at the headquarters of the said court in Sévaré, noted AMAP. Scheduled from 19 to 29 October, these hearings have 43 cases on the docket, involving 72 defendants including 69 military and 3 civilians .

article_manifest.title: Bamako: two suspects arrested in a burglary case involving more than 200 million FCFA
article_manifest.original_title: Bamako : deux suspects interpellés dans une affaire de cambriolages portant sur plus de 200 millions FCFA
article_manifest.summary: The Police Station of the Shopping Center arrested, on the night of October 14 to 15, 2026, two individuals suspected of being involved in several burglaries of shops in Bamako and its surroundings . The operation was conducted under the direction of Chief Commissioner Josué Kamaté, assisted by his deputy, Commissioner Issa Kouma. The investigation, opened following several complaints, made it possible to identify 14 businesses victims of these acts, for a declared damage of more than 200 million FCFA .

article_manifest.original_title: More than 40 civilians killed in Mali attack blamed on Islamic State

article_manifest.title: Uganda: Rwandan opponent in exile, Robert Kabera, found dead
article_manifest.original_title: Ouganda: l’opposant rwandais en exil, Robert Kabera, a été retrouvé mort
article_manifest.summary: Robert Kabera, 50, a Rwandan refugee in Uganda and a former non-commissioned officer in the Rwandan army who became an ardent critic of the government of Paul Kagame was found beheaded near the capital Kampala. The announcement was made on Monday, October 19, 2026 by the Ugandan police. Robert Kabera had fled his country Rwanda in November 2020 after he was accused of sexual assault, which he has always denied .

article_manifest.summary: Burkina/Justice: The death penalty reintroduced into the Penal Code, sanctions revised upwards The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, defended, this Tuesday, October 20, 2026 before the parliamentarians of the People's Legislative Assembly (Alp), the bill revising Law No. 025-2018/AN of May 25, 2018 on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso At the end of the votes, the Alp unanimously adopted the new law on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso, with the reintroduction of the death penalty (which had been abolished on 31 May 2018).

article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger have reopened formal discussions with the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), more than 18 months after leaving the regional organisation. The two sides agreed on Saturday to set up joint working groups to develop a framework for future cooperation, signalling renewed efforts to rebuild relations. The three countries, governed by military juntas, withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025 after establishing the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), following military coups and growing disagreements with the regional bloc.

article_manifest.title: Sahel: violent fighting between the jihadists of Jnim and those of the ISE at the Mali-Burkina border
article_manifest.original_title: Sahel: violents combats entre les jihadistes du Jnim et ceux de l'EIS à la frontière Mali-Burkina
article_manifest.summary: Sahel: violent fighting between the jihadists of Jnim and those of ISIS at the Mali-Burkina border Major fighting has been taking place since August between the jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda, and their rivals the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS). These fights are taking place on the border between Mali and Burkina Faso, also not far from the Nigerian border .

article_manifest.title: Nioro: a gesture of solidarity with the poorest
article_manifest.original_title: Nioro : un geste de solidarité envers les plus démunis
article_manifest.summary: In Nioro, elderly people, single women with family responsibilities, people living with disabilities and widows from the El Hadj Omar Tall military camp benefited from donations on Wednesday, October 14. Kits include millet, rice, oil, sugar, pasta and soap . The ceremony, organized as part of the Month of Solidarity and the Fight against Social Exclusion, ended with the presentation of certificates to the sponsors of the thematic weeks and the Month of Solidarity.

article_manifest.title: Two military operations targeting two armed positions in central Mali
article_manifest.original_title: عمليتان عسكريتان تستهدفان موقعين لمسلحين في وسط مالي
article_manifest.summary: On Thursday, the Malian army announced the targeting of two sites it said were sheltering armed men, one near the city of Diora and the other in the Ségou area, during two military operations on Wednesday and Thursday, without providing a toll of the losses. The army said in a statement that the first operation targeted a base 12 kilometers northwest of Diora, after being monitored based on intelligence information, noting that it included armed elements and military and logistical equipment.

article_manifest.title: Sectors of Dioura and Tongolo Coura: New terrorist bases targeted and destroyed by FAMa
article_manifest.original_title: Secteurs de Dioura et Tongolo Coura : De nouvelles bases terroristes ciblées et détruites par les FAMa
article_manifest.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On Wednesday, October 14, 2026, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, 12 kilometers northwest of the city of Dioura, a large base housing several terrorist elements as well as war and logistics equipment.

article_manifest.title: 04:10 Counter-terrorism: The FAMa neutralize two important terrorist bases in the regions of Dioura and Ségou
article_manifest.original_title: 04:10 Lutte contre le terrorisme : Les FAMa neutralisent deux importantes bases terroristes dans les régions de Dioura et Ségou
article_manifest.summary: A major logistics base northwest of Dioura and a terrorist assembly point near Tongolo Coura have been destroyed, the General Staff of the Armed Forces announced in a statement, while noting that surveillance and research operations continue on the ground . On Wednesday, October 14, 2026, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, 12 kilometers northwest of the city of Dioura, a large base housing several terrorist elements as well as war and logistics equipment.

article_manifest.title: Ransom, zakat, territory: the war between Jnim and the Islamic State is intensifying in the Sahel
article_manifest.original_title: Rançons, zakat, territoire : la guerre entre le Jnim et l’État islamique s’intensifie au Sahel
article_manifest.summary: Ransom, zakat, territory: the war between Jnim and the Islamic State intensifies in the Sahel On October 10, bloody fighting pitted Jnim against the Islamic State in Burkina Faso.

article_manifest.title: Why China won’t build its own Wagner in Africa
article_manifest.original_title: Why China won’t build its own Wagner in Africa
article_manifest.summary: Attacks on Chinese workers in Mali are testing Beijing’s reliance on African security forces. Russia’s experience there gives China little reason to take on the fighting itself. On 9 May, fighters from Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), al-Qaeda’s affiliate in the Sahel, stopped buses and trucks at Zambougou, in the Ségou region of Mali about 60 kilometres from Bamako, ordered the passengers out and burned at least 40 civilian vehicles.

article_manifest.title: Mali: The Army announces a tragic incident in an Fama area of operations
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : L’Armée annonce un incident tragique dans une zone d’opérations des FAMA
article_manifest.summary: In a statement issued yesterday, Wednesday, October 14, 2026, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Mali said that it had been informed of a "tragic incident that occurred in an area of operations". "Loss of life as well as injuries" are to be deplored According to the first administrative information available, the victims "travelled on heavy-duty motorcycles between two localities".

article_manifest.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
article_manifest.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: The FAMa hit two terrorist positions in Dioura and Ségou
article_manifest.original_title: Opération Dougoukoloko : Les FAMa frappent deux positions des terroristes à Dioura et à Ségou
article_manifest.summary: Bamako, October 15, 2026 (AMAP) - The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, successfully carried out two strikes against positions housing terrorist elements, respectively 12 kilometers northwest of Dioura and near Tongolo-Coura, in the Ségou region, the General Staff of the Armed Forces said in a statement released Thursday. According to the press release, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible, on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, to locate a large base housing several terrorist elements as well as war and logistics equipment, 12 kilometers northwest of the city of Dioura.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: Government pays tribute to Thomas Sankara, 39 years after his assassination
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso : le gouvernement rend hommage à Thomas Sankara, 39 ans après son assassinat
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso: the government pays tribute to Thomas Sankara, 39 years after his assassination Burkina Faso pays tribute, this Thursday, October 15, 2026, to Captain Thomas Isidore Noël Sankara and his 12 companions, murdered on October 15, 1987. The ceremony is held in Ouagadougou, in the presence of members of the government and administrative and customary authorities .

article_manifest.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: the FAMa strike two terrorist positions
article_manifest.original_title: Opération Dougoukoloko : les FAMa frappent deux positions terroristes
article_manifest.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, carried out two strikes against suspected terrorist positions on 14 and 15 October 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces . On Wednesday, October 14, a base housing combatants and war materiel was located 12 kilometers northwest of Dioura, thanks to intelligence.

article_manifest.title: Dr. Ahmadou Touré: "No sustainable development is possible without effective sovereignty"
article_manifest.original_title: Dr Ahmadou Touré : « Aucun développement durable n’est possible sans souveraineté effective »
article_manifest.summary: In his new book, "Sovereignty and State Refoundation in Mali (2020-2026): Towards the Alliance of Sahel States", professor-researcher Dr Ahmadou Touré analyses the trajectory opened in 2020. Assistant Professor and Director of the Sahel Governance, Mediation and Security Research Centre, he specifies the criteria for effective sovereignty and the conditions necessary for the consolidation of the ESA .

article_manifest.title: Kidal: After the army, reinstall the state
article_manifest.original_title: Kidal : Après l’armée, réinstaller l’État
article_manifest.summary: The FAMa took over Kidal on 6 October, almost six months after their withdrawal. Securing the city opens another project: restoring administration, bringing back public services and reconnecting with dispersed populations, while armed groups remain active. The Malian army has consolidated its presence after air and ground operations carried out as part of Operation Dougoukoloko .

article_manifest.title: Cybersecurity: Côte d 'Ivoire prepares its first national cyber crisis simulation
article_manifest.original_title: Cybersécurité : La Côte d’Ivoire prépare sa première simulation nationale de crise cyber
article_manifest.summary: Côte d 'Ivoire is preparing to organize its first national cyber crisis simulation. Called CYBER.EX 2026, this initiative will be held from 28 to 29 October 2026 at the Radisson Blu in Abidjan. Supported by the National Agency for the Security of Information Systems of Côte d 'Ivoire (ANSSI-CI), the event will bring together more than 800 participants around exercises intended to strengthen the response to cyber attacks .

article_manifest.title: Black October in Mali: when fear replaces solidarity
article_manifest.original_title: Octobre noir au Mali : quand la peur remplace la solidarité
article_manifest.summary: October is traditionally a month dedicated to solidarity and the fight against exclusion. It is also the month of Pink October, dedicated to raising awareness about breast cancer. A month that should rhyme with self-help, compassion and the protection of.

article_manifest.title: Diffa: Launch of a yellow fever vaccination campaign for nearly one million people
article_manifest.original_title: Diffa : Lancement d’une campagne de vaccination contre la fièvre jaune pour près d’un million de personnes
article_manifest.summary: Diffa, Oct 15 (ANP) – The Secretary General of the Diffa region, Mr. Mahamadou Attahirou Maidouka, on Thursday, October 15, 2026, at the Diffa Urban Integrated Health Center, officially launched the preventive vaccination campaign against yellow fever, scheduled for October 15 to 21 in the six departments of the region . This operation aims to vaccinate more than 95% of the target population, estimated at 999,877 people aged 9 months to 60 years.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso’s junta lays claim to Thomas Sankara’s legacy
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso’s junta lays claim to Thomas Sankara’s legacy
article_manifest.summary: A memorial to the assassinated revolutionary, conceived by his followers, is being remade by the Sahel state’s military leader, Ibrahim Traoré, who casts himself as Sankara’s heir.

article_manifest.title: AGADEZ: Regional Security Council meeting extended to members of the National Commission for the Collection and Control of Illicit Weapons
article_manifest.original_title: AGADEZ : Réunion du Conseil Régional de Sécurité élargie aux membres de la Commission Nationale pour la Collecte et le Contrôle des Armes illicites
article_manifest.summary: Agadez, Oct 15 (ANP) – The Governor of the Region of Agadez, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa chaired, this Thursday, October 15, 2026 in the meeting room of the Governorate, a meeting of the Regional Security Council (CRS) extended to members of the National Commission for the Collection and Control of Illicit Weapons (CNCCAI) . The CNCCAI plays a strategic role in the Regional Security Council, bringing together the defense forces to coordinate efforts to collect and control illicit weapons, which contributes to peace and security in the region.

article_manifest.title: Between Us: No one is safe
article_manifest.original_title: Entre Nous: Nul n’est à l’abri
article_manifest.summary: The National Human Rights Commission recalls that no one is immune from the violation of their rights. In Mali, outrage is often selective. Sponsors and implementers of extrajudicial abductions and kidnappings should know that they can become victims .

article_manifest.title: Dialogue forum: Civil society and security services meet around the same table
article_manifest.original_title: Forum de dialogue : Société civile et services de sécurité se retrouvent autour d'une même table
article_manifest.summary: Representatives of civil society and security actors met this Wednesday, October 14 in Bamako, for the Community Dialogue Forum on Security Sector Governance . The opening ceremony was chaired by the representative of the Commissioner for Security Sector Reform (C-RSS), in the presence of Philipp Schweers, Acting Head of Mission of EUCAP Sahel Mali, the representative of the Governor of the District of Bamako, as well as representatives of pea and WANEP-Mali .

article_manifest.title: 7-October: Benyamin Netanyahu attacked in defamation by the former head of the Shin Beth
article_manifest.original_title: 7-Octobre: Benyamin Netanyahu attaqué en diffamation par l'ancien chef du Shin Beth
article_manifest.summary: For weeks, revelations have been going on in Israel to say that Benyamin Netanyahu did not follow up on alerts and warnings from foreign countries but also from his own security services concerning 7-October. Two weeks before the elections, the former head of the Shin Beth attacked the Prime Minister for defamation . He accuses her of lying about their respective responsibilities.

article_manifest.title: NSCDC arrest 2 over abortions, trafficking
article_manifest.original_title: NSCDC arrest 2 over abortions, trafficking
article_manifest.summary: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has arrested a 22-year-old man for allegedly trafficking a 17-year-old girl from Kwara State to Mali after promising to secure her employment in Senegal. The command also arrested a 56-year-old man accused of operating an unauthorised medical facility and performing abortions without recognised medical qualifications or a valid licence.

article_manifest.title: Africa: In Mali, From the Wagner Group to Africa Corps - Will Impunity Continue?
article_manifest.original_title: Africa: In Mali, From the Wagner Group to Africa Corps - Will Impunity Continue?
article_manifest.summary: When Africa Corps officially began operations in Mali in June 2025, few people held out hope that it would help alleviate the suffering of civilians in Mali, caused on the one hand by armed groups in Azawad and members from the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), but also by the army and its auxiliaries from the Russian private military company known as Wagner.

article_manifest.title: National Youth Service: 2,400 recruits of the 7th cohort ready to serve The ceremony of their presentation to the flag was chaired, yesterday, on the place d 'armes of the Military Engineer, by the President of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goïta . For six months, these men and women followed a demanding program of military and civic training that allowed them to learn how to transform fatigue into endurance, difficulties into courage and constraints into responsibilities
article_manifest.original_title: Service national des jeunes : 2.400 recrues de la 7è cohorte prêtes à servir La cérémonie de leur présentation au drapeau a été présidée, hier, sur la place d’armes du Génie militaire, par le Président de la Transition, le Général d’armée Assimi Goïta. Pendant six mois, ces hommes et ces femmes ont suivi un programme exigeant de formation militaire et civique qui leur a permis d’apprendre à transformer la fatigue en endurance, les difficultés en courage et les contraintes en responsabilités
article_manifest.summary: This cohort includes 573 non-public servants and 1,827 civil servants. The 7th cohort of the National Youth Service (SNJ), composed of 2,400 recruits from the first and second waves, completed six months of military and civic training at the Bapho Training Center . The ceremony of presentation to the flag, presided over by the president of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goïta, took place yesterday at the Place d 'Armes of the Military Engineer, in an atmosphere of emotion and patriotic pride .

article_manifest.title: Niger: an ordinance specifies the missions of the Human Rights Observatory
article_manifest.original_title: Niger : une ordonnance précise les missions de l’Observatoire des droits de l’Homme
article_manifest.summary: The President of Niger, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, signed on October 14, 2026 an order relating to the National Observatory for Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ONDH/LF), an institution provided for by Article 72 of the Charter of Refoundation, according to a statement from the General Secretariat of the Government . Responsible for the promotion and protection of human rights, the Observatory will carry out regular, announced or unannounced visits to places of detention, with the exception of the State Security Council.

article_manifest.title: Niger has set up a National Observatory on Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms
article_manifest.original_title: Le Niger se dote d’un Observatoire National des Droits de l’ Homme et des Libertés Fondamentales
article_manifest.summary: Niamey, October 14 (ANP)- The President of the Republic, Head of State, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, signed, on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, an order creating a National Observatory of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ONDH/LF) . The National Observatory for Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, it is stated, is an institution provided for in Article 72 of the Charter of the Refoundation and has the mission of protecting and promoting human rights .

article_manifest.title: Niamey denounces the expulsion of two agents by Paris
article_manifest.original_title: Niamey dénonce l’expulsion de deux agents par Paris
article_manifest.summary: The Nigerien government strongly criticized, on Tuesday, the expulsion by France of two Nigerien agents declared persona non grata on September 16, 2026. Niamey views this decision as a “serious and unacceptable act of ingratitude,” said Justice Minister Alio Daouda According to the Nigerien Minister of Justice, one of the two agents expelled by Paris, Abdoul-Razak Ibrahim Moussa Toro, was wounded in 2014 during a mission to Diffa, in south-eastern Niger, in cooperation with the French army.

article_manifest.title: Dougabougou: A municipal councillor murdered in his home by armed men
article_manifest.original_title: Dougabougou : Un conseiller communal assassiné à son domicile par des hommes armés
article_manifest.summary: A communal councillor, named Mohamed Arby, was killed by unidentified armed men on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, at his home in Dougabougou, in the Ségou region.

article_manifest.title: Niger: Tebboune strengthens military contacts in the Sahel
article_manifest.original_title: Niger : Tebboune renforce les contacts militaires au Sahel
article_manifest.summary: Behind the speech of regional solidarity displayed by Algiers on the occasion of the reception of the Nigerien Minister of Defence, the contradictions of Algerian policy in the Sahel question the real scope of its commitment to regional stability . The reception, Tuesday, October 13 in Algiers, of the Nigerien Minister of Defense by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune comes in a context of recomposition of Sahelian alliances, marked by tensions between Algeria and several countries in the region .

article_manifest.title: Mali-Côte d 'Ivoire: relaunch of Security Cooperation
article_manifest.original_title: Mali-Côte d’Ivoire : relance de la Coopération sécuritaire
article_manifest.summary: Intelligence cooperation and the fight against terrorism: the visit to Bamako of Vassiriki Traoré, the national intelligence coordinator of Côte d 'Ivoire, should revolve around these themes. A trip "at the invitation of the director of the National Intelligence Agency of Mali, General Modibo Koné", according to the security services of Mali. Vassiriki Traoré should be received by President Assimi Goïta .

article_manifest.original_title: Autisme au Burkina Faso : le combat des parents contre les préjugés

article_manifest.title: Mali: National Youth Service recruits presented to the flag
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : les recrues du Service national des jeunes présentées au drapeau
article_manifest.summary: The 7th cohort of the National Youth Service (SNJ) of Mali was presented to the flag on October 13, 2026 in Bamako, during a ceremony presided over by the president of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, announces the Malian presidency. Composed of 2,400 recruits, including 1,827 civil servants and 573 non-officials, from various professional backgrounds, this promotion also includes 800 women, according to the same source .

article_manifest.title: In Mali, the army recognizes a half-word blunder
article_manifest.original_title: Au Mali, l’armée reconnaît une bavure à demi-mot
article_manifest.summary: A strike in Mali killed nearly ten people, including women and children, on October 12. Usually quick to deny the collateral damage, the Malian army acknowledged without precision a "tragic incident". Is this the first sign of a recognition of the cost of war borne by civilians?

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: Captain Ibrahim Traoré appoints new leaders at the head of the Rapid Intervention Groups (GIR)
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré nomme de nouveaux chefs à la tête des Groupements d’Intervention Rapide (GIR)
article_manifest.summary: After the establishment of the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR), the Head of State, Comrade Captain Ibrahim Traoré, continued the restructuring of the Burkinabe army with the creation of a new counter-terrorism mechanism: the Rapid Intervention Groups (GIR). In a decree signed on 23 September 2026, he appointed new heads of these units Under the authority of the Special and Rapid Intervention Brigade (BSIR), the mission of the Rapid Intervention Groups (GIR) is to strengthen the operational capacities of the armed forces in the fight against terrorism and organized crime in Burkina Faso.

article_manifest.title: Mali: army investigates deadly incident in military zone
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : l’armée enquête sur un incident meurtrier en zone militaire
article_manifest.summary: The General Staff of the Malian Armed Forces reported, on October 14, 2026, an incident that caused loss of life and injuries in an area of military operations. But for now, the circumstances of the tragedy remain to be established, while the authorities maintain restrictions on the movement of large cylinders . The Malian army is seeking to determine the circumstances of a deadly incident in an area of military operations that has reported deaths and injuries .

article_manifest.title: Mali: the General Staff calls for respect of the restrictions on the movement of large cylinders
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : l’État-major appelle au respect des restrictions de circulation des grosses cylindrées
article_manifest.summary: Mali: the General Staff calls for respect of restrictions on the movement of large vehicles The General Staff of the Armed Forces announced a tragic incident in an area of operations, resulting in deaths and injuries. According to initial information, the victims were travelling on large motorcycles between two localities. The exact circumstances of the event remain to be established In a statement, the command extended its condolences to the bereaved families and wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

article_manifest.title: Mali: Nduhungirehe, Mali President Discuss Bilateral Relations
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: Nduhungirehe, Mali President Discuss Bilateral Relations

article_manifest.title: Expulsion of Nigerien agents by Paris: Niamey denounces a "serious and unacceptable act of ingratitude"

article_manifest.title: Yélimané: three suspects arrested for a fake gold scam
article_manifest.original_title: Yélimané : trois suspects arrêtés pour une arnaque au faux or
article_manifest.summary: As part of the "Kokadjè" operation, the Yélimané police station arrested three people on October 9 and 10, 2026. They are suspected of having defrauded several victims by selling them zinc presented as gold After several complaints, the Search Brigade arrested two suspects, I.C., 25, and O.C., 18, on October 9 in Djadji, about one kilometer from Yélimané. According to the first elements of the investigation, they gave zinc to their victims by passing it off as a precious metal.

article_manifest.title: Zinc Scam Sold for Gold: Three Suspects Arrested by Yélimané Police
article_manifest.original_title: Arnaque au zinc vendu pour de l’or : Trois suspects arrêtés par la police de Yélimané
article_manifest.summary: FIGHT AGAINST DELINQUENCY and CRIME: As part of the "Kokadjè" operation, carried out at the instigation of the Regional Director of the National Police of Kayes, the Chief Police Controller Tapa Oury DIALLO, the Yélimané Police Station, headed by the Chief Police Commissioner Adama KODIO, proceeded, between 9 and 10 October 2026, to arrest three (03) individuals suspected of having defrauded several people by masquerading zinc as gold.

article_manifest.title: Road tragedy at the entrance to Ségou: A young officer loses his life in a three-vehicle collision

article_manifest.original_title: 'Act of ingratitude': Niger condemns expulsion of security agents from France
article_manifest.summary: Niger on Tuesday condemned the expulsion of two of its security agents from France, calling it a “serious and unacceptable act of ingratitude.” The diplomatic row began last month when Paris declared the two men personae non grata. According to French media reports, their expulsion was related to suspicions they were monitoring Nigerien opposition figures in France.

article_manifest.title: Sahel: The number of displaced in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger has almost doubled since 2020, according to UNHCR
article_manifest.original_title: Sahel: le nombre de déplacés au Burkina Faso, au Mali et au Niger a presque doublé depuis 2020, selon le HCR
article_manifest.summary: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) warns of the displacement crisis in the Sahel: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger now have nearly 4 million displaced persons and refugees, almost twice as many as in 2020, the year of the first military coup in Bamako . Published on: In Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, “security incidents have nearly doubled since 2020, weakening the state presence […] and increasing risks for both displaced people and host communities,” said Abdouraouf Gnon-Konde, UNHCR's Director for West and Central Africa, on Friday, 9 October .

article_manifest.title: Niger: Niger Intelligence Agents Expelled From France in Sign of Diplomatic Strain
article_manifest.original_title: Niger: Niger Intelligence Agents Expelled From France in Sign of Diplomatic Strain
article_manifest.summary: Two Nigerien intelligence officers were forced to leave France last month, French daily Le Monde has revealed, with one agent suspected of monitoring opposition figures on French soil. It is the latest sign of the deterioration in relations between the two countries since Niger's 2023 military coup. France expelled two Nigerien intelligence officers posted at Niger's embassy in Paris last month, a diplomatic source told French news agency AFP.

article_manifest.title: Fuel supply: 5,396 tankers arrived in Bamako since September
article_manifest.original_title: Approvisionnement en carburant : 5 396 camions-citernes arrivés à Bamako depuis septembre
article_manifest.summary: Fuel supply: 5,396 tanker trucks arrived in Bamako since September A new convoy of 957 tanker trucks arrived in Bamako this Saturday, October 10, 2026, under the escort of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), according to the Directorate General of Trade, Consumption and Competition (DGCC). In September, the capital recorded the arrival of 3,796 tanker trucks divided into five convoys .

article_manifest.title: Burkina: suspension of flour exports
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina : suspension des exportations de farine
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso has suspended until further notice the export of millet, maize and sorghum flour, as well as their derivatives, to ensure their availability on the national market, according to an official statement consulted on Saturday . A measure to freeze exports of millet, maize and sorghum flour was announced by the Burkinabe authorities in a press release dated 9 October and signed by the Minister of Industry, Trade and Handicrafts, Serge Gnaniodem Poda.

article_manifest.title: Traditional chieftaincy: Mr. Bachir Sadou Kalilou elected 16th chief of canton of Sakoira
article_manifest.original_title: Chefferie traditionnelle : M. Bachir Sadou Kalilou élu 16ᵉ chef de canton de Sakoira
article_manifest.summary: Tillabéri, 10 Oct (ANP) – Mr. Bachir Sadou Kalilou, was elected this Saturday, October 10, 2026, unanimously by his peers, 16th head of canton of Sakoira, a rural commune attached to the department of Tillabéri .

article_manifest.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
article_manifest.title: Tenenkou: 14 tons of food will be distributed to 231 vulnerable households
article_manifest.original_title: Tenenkou : 14 tonnes de vivres seront distribuées à 231 ménages vulnérables
article_manifest.summary: Tenenkou, 10 October (AMAP) A total of 14 tonnes of millet will be distributed to 231 vulnerable households, or 1,389 beneficiaries in the urban commune of Tenenkou, as part of the national food insecurity response plan. The launch ceremony of this operation was held Saturday in front of the town hall, under the chairmanship of the 2nd deputy to the prefect, the Chief Commissioner of Police Ousmane Diamouténé, noted AMAP .

article_manifest.title: Mali.. Army targets two vehicles in Kidal and Timbuktu base
article_manifest.original_title: مالي.. الجيش يستهدف مركبتين في كيدال وقاعدة بتمبكتو
article_manifest.summary: The Malian Army announced the targeting of two vehicles that it said were transporting "armed elements" southwest of Kidal city, in addition to carrying out an airstrike that targeted a base that includes armed elements and military and logistical equipment in the Ndaki area in Timbuktu state. He said in a statement issued on Friday evening that the two vehicles were spotted 45 and 46 kilometers southwest of Kidal during the ongoing military operations in the eastern region.

article_manifest.title: GOONGA TAN: Kidal: the return of the flag, the return
article_manifest.original_title: GOONGA TAN : Kidal : le retour du drapeau, le retour
article_manifest.summary: Mali finds Kidal. But beyond a military victory, it is a political, historical and symbolic battle that changes its nature. Indeed, this Tuesday, October 6, 2026 will undoubtedly remain as one of the highlights of Mali's recent history .

article_manifest.title: Mali: The national flag now flies in the sky of Kidal
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : Le drapeau national flotte désormais dans le ciel de Kidal
article_manifest.summary: Kidal, the strategic city in northern Mali has been back in the fold of the state since Tuesday, October 6, 2026. The Malian Armed Forces (Fama) and their Russian allies have indeed managed to take control of this megalopolis after a major military offensive . To mark the total and entire membership of the Ifoghas city in the Republic of Mali, the national flag was raised on its public buildings.

article_manifest.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: FAMa strike hard in Kidal and Timbuktu
article_manifest.original_title: Opération Dougoukoloko : Les FAMa frappent fort à Kidal et Tombouctou
article_manifest.summary: Operation Dougoukoloko: FAMa strikes hard in Kidal and Timbuktu Two surgical strikes conducted by FAMa, with the support of their partners, neutralized terrorist elements in the Eastern and Central regions as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. Eastern Theater: This Friday, October 9, 2026, two vehicles carrying terrorists were spotted 45 and 46 km southwest of Kidal .

article_manifest.title: Zinder: eleven suspects arrested after the dismantling of two criminal networks
article_manifest.original_title: Zinder : onze suspects interpellés après le démantèlement de deux réseaux criminels
article_manifest.summary: Eleven individuals arrested, fifteen victims identified and three people actively wanted: the dismantling of two criminal networks by the Zinder Interregional Criminal Police Service reveals serial robberies in homes and markets, as well as a concealment circuit linking Zinder, Maradi and the surroundings of Takeita. The case started with an abandoned motorcycle in the Jacques Chirac district of Zinder .

article_manifest.title: 7 Mali: The takeover of Kidal "consolidates" the Transition
article_manifest.original_title: 7 Mali: La reprise de Kidal «consolide» la Transition
article_manifest.summary: In Mali, the army and its Russian partners of the Africa Corps reinvested Tuesday, October 6, the city of Kidal, in the north of the country, less than six months after being driven out by the separatists of the Fla and their jihadist allies of the Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda. This prestigious victory was achieved without even having to fight, as the armed groups withdrew before the arrival of the army .

article_manifest.summary: BAMAKO and Algiers talk again. Ambassadors have returned, diplomatic borders are reopening and a visit by General Assimi Goïta to Algeria is announced. Good!

article_manifest.title: GAO: 234 trainees complete their Inter-Arms Certificate (CIA) training
article_manifest.original_title: GAO : 234 stagiaires achèvent leur formation au Certificat Interarmes (CIA)
article_manifest.summary: The Gao Mixed Instruction Center hosted, on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, the ceremony of end of training of the first wave of the Joint Certificate (CIA), session 2025, started on July 10, 2026. For three months, 234 trainees from the Defence and Security Forces underwent training to strengthen their military knowledge and skills . At the end of this course, they are now able to assume the functions of deputy non-commissioned officer to the section head.

article_manifest.title: DIRECTORATE OF THE ARMED FORCES COMMISSARIAT: The Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces on an official visit
article_manifest.original_title: DIRECTION DU COMMISSARIAT DES ARMÉES : Le Chef d’État-Major Général des Armées en visite d’autorité
article_manifest.summary: The Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces (CEMGA), Major General Elisée Jean DAO, visited the Directorate of the Commissariat of the Armed Forces (DCA), formerly Military Headquarters, on Friday, October 9, 2026. This visit is a continuation of the authority visits made by the CMSA to the various service directorates of the Malian Armed Forces since his appointment as head of the institution in May .

article_manifest.title: Court remands Nigerien man in Abuja for alleged supply of AK-47 ammunition for terrorism
article_manifest.original_title: Court remands Nigerien man in Abuja for alleged supply of AK-47 ammunition for terrorism
article_manifest.summary: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday remanded a Nigerien national, Muhammad Ibrahim, over charges of transporting 170 rounds of AK-47 ammunition for terrorist activities in Katsina State. Judge Salim Ibrahim ordered that Mr Ibrahim be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre in Abuja after he pleaded not guilty to four counts, including terrorism and fraudulent acquisition of a Nigerian identification number – the National Identity Number (NIN).

article_manifest.title: Nobel Peace Prize 2026: Africa in the spotlight with South Africa's Navi Pillay
article_manifest.original_title: Nobel de la paix 2026 : l’Afrique à l’honneur avec la Sud-Africaine Navi Pillay
article_manifest.summary: Africa is in the spotlight on the international scene. South Africa's Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday, October 9, 2026. This distinction highlights the journey of an African woman committed to defending human rights and respecting international law Former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and former judge at the International Criminal Court (ICC), she has distinguished herself by her fight against impunity and for justice.

article_manifest.title: Mali: In Kidal, soldiers outnumber locals
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: à Kidal, les soldats sont plus nombreux que les habitants
article_manifest.summary: Mali: in Kidal, the soldiers outnumber the inhabitants Three days after their return to Kidal, the Malian soldiers and their Russian partners of the Africa Corps secure the city and its surroundings. The army conducts daily airstrikes in the area but has not yet continued its ground advance The separatists of the Azawad Liberation Front (Fla) and the jihadists of the Support Group for Islam and Muslims (Jnim), linked to al-Qaeda, were forced to withdraw before the arrival of the army in Kidal.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: The export of millet, maize and sorghum flour suspended until further notice
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso : L’exportation des farines de mil, de maïs et de sorgho suspendue jusqu’à nouvel ordre
article_manifest.summary: The Burkinabe government suspends, until further notice, the export of millet, maize and sorghum flour, as well as their derivatives, throughout the national territory. The measure aims to ensure the availability of these products on the internal market and to improve their accessibility to consumers . In a press release dated 9 October 2026, the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Handicrafts informed economic operators and populations of this decision.

article_manifest.title: In Mali, the recapture of the city of Kidal offers a symbolic victory to the junta and its Russian ally
article_manifest.original_title: Au Mali, la reprise de la ville de Kidal offre une victoire symbolique à la junte et à son allié russe
article_manifest.summary: In Mali, the recapture of the city of Kidal offers a symbolic victory to the junta and its DECRYPTING Russian ally - The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian mercenaries and Tuareg loyalists, have taken over this rebel-held city since a general offensive in April. On November 14, 2023, during the first conquest of Kidal by the Malian army with the support of Wagner, the Russian mercenaries, enlisted by the ruling junta, had raised their black flag with a death's head.

article_manifest.title: Resumption of Kidal: place for the security and effective return of state services
article_manifest.original_title: Reprise de Kidal : place à la sécurisation et au retour effectif des services de l’État
article_manifest.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) consolidated their presence in Kidal on 6 October 2026, at the end of military operations carried out as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, with the support of their Russian partners. This breakthrough is an important step . The sustainable security of the city, the protection of the population and the effective return of state services are now major issues.

article_manifest.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
article_manifest.title: Gao: Trial of nine (9) criminal cases involving 11 defendants
article_manifest.original_title: Gao : jugement de neuf (9) affaires criminelles impliquant 11 accusés
article_manifest.summary: Gao, 9 October (AMAP) The first session of the criminal chamber of the Gao High Court ended on 8 October 2026 in the City of Askias, noted AMAP . Started on October 6, this series of hearings aimed to deal with 9 major criminal cases involving a total of 11 defendants including the nature of the cases examined and all judged at the very first hearing of the criminal chamber of the Gao High Court, namely 2 murders, 3 pedophilia, 2 fatal strokes, 1 rape and 1 murder During these hearings, the Criminal Chamber of the Gao TGI pronounced sanctions commensurate with the criminal offences committed.

article_manifest.title: Fama takeover of Kidal: Choguel Maiga's reaction
article_manifest.original_title: Prise de Kidal par les FAMA : La réaction de Choguel Maiga
article_manifest.summary: Capture of Kidal by the Fama: Choguel Maiga Kidal's reaction is no longer in the hands of the terrorists. This strategic town in northern Mali was recaptured by the Malian Armed Forces (Fama) on October 6, after a vast military offensive carried out with the support of the Russian partners of Africorps. From the prison of Koulikoro, the former Malian Prime Minister Choguel Maiga congratulated the FAMa for their shine .

article_manifest.title: West Africa: Russia-Ukraine Conflict Finds New Battleground in Africa's Sahel
article_manifest.original_title: West Africa: Russia-Ukraine Conflict Finds New Battleground in Africa's Sahel
article_manifest.summary: Ukraine has vowed to counter Russia wherever it can, even "in the scorching sands" of the Sahelian desert, as evidence mounts that Kyiv is backing Tuareg separatists battling Mali's army and its Russian allies. Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso -- all led by military juntas that have turned their backs on former colonial ruler France and moved closer to Russia -- have reacted by severing diplomatic relations with Kyiv.

article_manifest.title: South Africa: the army deployed after xenophobic violence
article_manifest.original_title: Afrique du Sud : l’armée déployée après des violences xénophobes
article_manifest.summary: Police and the army were deployed Friday in Durban and Soweto after anti-immigration protests turned violent, leaving at least 24 vehicles burned and several businesses owned by foreigners targeted. South African authorities have stepped up their security presence in both cities to prevent further violence, in the wake of clashes between South African protesters and foreign nationals.

article_manifest.title: Mali: "The army has its place in Kidal but regaining it does not end the violence", for the opposition coalition CFR
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: «L'armée a sa place à Kidal mais la reconquérir ne met pas fin aux violences», pour la coalition d'opposition CFR
article_manifest.summary: In Mali, the army and its Russian partners in the Africa Corps retook Kidal in the north on 6 October from the Fla separatists and the Jnim jihadists, who had controlled it for more than five months. A victory for the transitional authorities who intend to restore the authority of the State throughout the territory . The CFR, a coalition of opponents in exile, also defends national sovereignty throughout the territory but advocates dialogue with armed groups.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: The junta tries to relax with the Sunnis
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso: La junte tente une décrispation avec les sunnites
article_manifest.summary: The release this Sunday, October 4, 2026, of approximately 80 supporters of Imam Mohamed Kindo is a political signal. Arrested at the end of May after a banned demonstration, shaved, and sent for training at the police camp, they are returning to their families. With video evidence, the junta is carefully staging a display of appeasement.

article_manifest.title: "Epic of Niger", a project by cultural entrepreneur Ibrahima Abdoul-Rachid: "It is enough for a people to turn to their memory for the future to change"
article_manifest.original_title: « Épopée du Niger », un projet de l’entrepreneur culturel Ibrahima Abdoul-Rachid : « Il suffit qu’un peuple se tourne vers sa mémoire pour que l’avenir change »
article_manifest.summary: Through the ecological company A.S.I.D., founded in 2020 and continuously active, Mr. Soumaila Ibrahima Abdoul-Rachid, cultural entrepreneur, proposes innovative and multisectoral initiatives combining ecology, digital and culture . This includes waste recovery such as the transformation of used tyres into urban and school furniture, edutainment projects, as well as the production of major cultural and transmedia works that strengthen the memory and intellectual sovereignty of the Nigerien public.

article_manifest.title: Talhandak, Kidal and Tessalit: Terrorist Positions Targeted and Accurately Addressed
article_manifest.original_title: Talhandak, Kidal et Tessalit : Des positions terroristes ciblées et traitées avec précision ACTUALITES
article_manifest.summary: The announcement was made on October 7, 2026 by the General Staff of the Armed Forces which indicates that in the continuity of the offensive launched in the East Theater, the air-land operations conducted today made it possible to precisely target several positions of the armed terrorist groups . On the ground, according to the security source, the responsiveness of the units made it possible to obtain convincing results, in particular in Talhandak, where terrorist elements who had sheltered under a canopy were neutralized and their vehicle completely destroyed .

article_manifest.title: Mali: "The army has its place in Kidal but regaining it does not end the violence", for the opposition coalition CFR
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: «L'armée a sa place à Kidal mais la reconquérir ne met pas fin aux violences», pour la coalition d'opposition CFR
article_manifest.summary: Mali: "The army has its place in Kidal but reconquering it does not end the violence", for the opposition coalition CFR In Mali, the army and its Russian partners of the Africa Corps took over Kidal, in the North, from the Fla separatists and the Jnim jihadists, who had controlled it for more than five months. A victory for the transitional authorities who intend to restore the authority of the State throughout the territory .

article_manifest.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: FAMa precision strikes against terrorist bases in San, Takalot and Talhandak
article_manifest.original_title: Opération Dougoukoloko : Frappes de précision des FAMa contre des bases terroristes à San, Takalot et Talhandak
article_manifest.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko In the continuation of the offensive launched in the Eastern Theater, the air-land operations conducted on Thursday, October 8, 2026 made it possible to target several positions of the armed terrorist groups.

article_manifest.title: Niger: Niger's Junta Tightens Its Grip On Free Expression
article_manifest.original_title: Niger: Niger's Junta Tightens Its Grip On Free Expression
article_manifest.summary: Lawyer Tried on Bogus Charges; Journalist Feared Forcibly Disappeared A lawyer in Niger faces prosecution over comments about the army on social media while a prominent journalist and critic of the country's military junta is being held in secret, with authorities refusing to identify his alleged offense. These cases together highlight a broadening crackdown in Niger, where the space for free expression is shrinking by the day.

article_manifest.title: Saddam Haftar: from the Sahel to Chad, the limits of security diplomacy
article_manifest.original_title: Saddam Haftar : du Sahel au Tchad, les limites d’une diplomatie sécuritaire
article_manifest.summary: Saddam Haftar: from the Sahel to Chad, the limits of a security diplomacy Between the release of hostages, support for rebel movements and a new alliance with Chad, Marshal Haftar's heir seeks to establish himself as an essential interlocutor. And dreams as a future president of a reunified Libya that would weigh again on continental diplomacy. Published today at 07:00, modified at 10:11 Reading: 10 minutes .

article_manifest.title: No to family war!
article_manifest.original_title: Non à la guerre familiale !
article_manifest.summary: We have VDPs on the battlefield against the forces of evil, but who are the VDPs in our families and where are they? We have been at war against terrorism for a decade but in our families, we shoot each other with live ammunition and at close range, among blood brothers, sometimes in deafening silence, sometimes with an unprecedented noise that attracts crowds .

article_manifest.title: ‎ Burkina Faso: The export of millet, maize and sorghum flour suspended until further notice
article_manifest.original_title: ‎ Burkina Faso : L’exportation de la farine de mil, de maïs et de sorgho suspendue jusqu’à nouvel ordre
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso: The export of millet, maize and sorghum flour suspended until further notice The export of cereal flour, including millet, maize and sorghum, as well as their derivatives, is suspended throughout the national territory until further notice. The information comes from a press release from the Minister of Trade, Industry and Handicrafts dated October 9, 2026 .

article_manifest.title: Month of Solidarity: President Assimi GOÏTA with the Dean of Bamako The inhabitants of the Troukabougou sector of Djicoroni Para, in Commune IV of the District of Bamako, woke up this Thursday, October 8, 2026 under an impressive security device.
article_manifest.original_title: Mois de la solidarité : Le Président Assimi GOÏTA chez le doyen de Bamako Les habitants du secteur Troukabougou de Djicoroni Para, en Commune IV du District de Bamako, se sont réveillés, ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026 sous un impressionnant dispositif de sécurité.
article_manifest.summary: Very early in the morning, the staking of the elements of the Security Forces announced that this district would welcome a distinguished host, including the President of the Transition, Army General Assimi Goïta, who sacrificed to a well-established tradition of the Month of Solidarity and the Fight against Exclusion, that is to say the visit of the highest authorities to the elderly It was in this spirit that the Head of State went to the bedside of the Dean of Bamako, Namory Keita.

article_manifest.title: In Mali, why the takeover of Kidal is a bitter-tasting victory for the junta
article_manifest.original_title: Au Mali, pourquoi la reprise de Kidal est une victoire au goût amer pour la junte
article_manifest.summary: It had been several days since a scent of reconquest floated in the air. On the morning of Tuesday, October 6, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian elements of Africa Corps, retook the city of Kidal In a statement dated the same day, the Malian military authorities announced that they had engaged in "large-scale air-land operations in the Kidal region" with a view to "neutralizing armed terrorist groups" and "destroying their sanctuaries".

article_manifest.title: Terrorists’ Illicit Funding Streams Converge
article_manifest.original_title: Terrorists’ Illicit Funding Streams Converge
article_manifest.summary: Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) amasses an estimated $100 million a year through a web of illicit activities that illustrates the way terrorism, organized crime and public corruption are connected. “Make no mistake, today illicit economies in the Sahel and West Africa are interlinked criminalities across borders,” David M. Luna, executive director of the International Coalition Against Illicit Economies (ICAIE), told a recent webinar hosted by the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).
